blocks.task_summary: Show that the two lines l₁ and l₂ do not intersect.
method_path: Set at least two components of l₁ and l₂ equal to form a system of linear equations in λ and μ
Attempt to solve two of the equations
Obtain a contradiction (e.g. 5 = 2), proving no solution exists
Conclude that l₁ and l₂ do not intersect
accepted_alternatives: Recognize that direction vectors (2,−2,2) and (1,−1,1) are scalar multiples, so lines are parallel; subtract position vectors to get (1,2,−5) and show it is not a scalar multiple of the direction vector, proving lines are distinct and do not intersect.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: 'setting at least two components of l1 and l2 equal' M1; 'attempt to solve two of the equations' M1; 'gives a contradiction (no solution), eg 5=2' R1; 'so l1 and l2 do not intersect AG' [3 marks]

METHOD 2: 'l1 and l2 are parallel, so l1 and l2 are either identical or distinct.' R1; 'Attempt to subtract two position vectors from each line' M1; showing resulting vector is not a multiple of direction vector A1 [3 marks]

blocks.task_summary: Find the minimum distance between the two parallel lines l₁ and l₂.
method_path: Note that l₁ and l₂ are parallel (direction vectors are scalar multiples)
Pick point A(3,2,−1) on l₁ and point B(2,0,4) on l₂
Compute cross product AB × v where v = (1,−1,1), obtaining (3, 6, 3)
Divide by |v| = √3 to obtain minimum distance = 3√2 = √18
accepted_alternatives: Let A be fixed on l₁, B general on l₂; express |AB|² = 3μ² + 12μ + 30; minimize by derivative d|AB|²/dμ = 6μ + 12 = 0 → μ = −2, or complete square 3(μ+2)²+18; minimum distance = √18 = 3√2.
Use dot-product condition AB·v = 0 with AB expressed in terms of μ (or λ); solve for μ = −2 or λ = 1; compute minimum distance = √18 = 3√2.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: 'l1 and l2 are parallel'; 'let A be (3,2,−1) on l1 and let B be (2,0,4) on l2'; 'Attempt to find vector AB = (−1,−2,5)' (M1); 'Distance required is |AB × v|/|v|' M1; cross product = (3,6,3) (A1); 'minimum distance is √18 = 3√2' A1 [5 marks]

METHOD 2: 'let A be a fixed point on l1 eg (3,2,−1) and let B be a general point on l2 (2+μ,−μ,4+μ)'; 'attempt to find vector AB' (M1); AB = (−1+μ,−2−μ,5+μ) A1; |AB|² = 3μ²+12μ+30 M1; derivative or completing square → μ=−2 A1; 'minimum distance is √18 = 3√2' A1 [5 marks]
METHOD 3: 'let A be (3,2,−1) on l1 and let B be (2+μ,−μ,4+μ) on l2' (M1); AB = (−1+μ,−2−μ,5+μ) A1; dot product AB·v = 0 → μ=−2 (or λ=1) M1, A1; 'minimum distance is √18 = 3√2' A1 [5 marks]
